name: Live-Action Whitespace Text Integration
use_when: Text needs to appear inside live-action footage without feeling pasted on.
A cinematic, ad, documentary, or social shot has negative space that can hold a label or title.
Scene text should support emotion, time, location, or proof while preserving the shot.
avoid_when: There is no clean negative space and text would cover the subject or proof.
The font theme clashes with the scene tone.
The edit would perform better with simple captions or a separate card instead of integrated scene text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: scan_frame -> identify_subject_and_negative_space -> choose_theme_matched_font -> match_temperature_and_contrast -> optional_track_or_anchor -> read_hold -> clear
timeline_pattern.negative_space_rule: Place text in unused frame space, not over the emotional focal point, product, lamp, face, hands, UI, or evidence.
timeline_pattern.temperature_rule: Use text color that belongs to the frame's warm/cool temperature unless deliberate contrast is the point.
timeline_pattern.theme_rule: A spooky, luxury, tech, handmade, or documentary scene needs matching type tone.
timeline_pattern.tracking_rule: Track or anchor text only when it should belong to the shot's space.

motion.rule: Integrated text can stay still, softly fade, or track with the scene; avoid loud motion that breaks emotion.

keyframe_values.soft_fade: Use a short opacity fade when hard text cuts distract from the scene.
keyframe_values.tracking_check: Review tracked text at full speed and delivery size to catch drift or jitter.

sound.rule: Use no SFX for subtle cinematic text unless the text is a story beat or transition.

captions.rule: Keep captions away from scene-attached text; if both are needed, assign separate safe regions and hierarchy.

color.rule: Match color temperature and contrast to the frame while preserving readability; do not blend text so much that viewers miss it.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawtext with explicit x/y safe regions, optional shadow/box, and precomputed tracking data for simple locked-off shots.
implementation.remotion: Model sceneText with anchorRegion, temperatureMatch, zIndex, trackData, safeRegion, and captionCollision fields.
implementation.blender: Use camera tracking or 3D text planes for scene-attached typography that should live in the shot.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place text in negative space, match font/theme/color, use tracking or keyframes only when needed, and preview for subject collisions.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics, guides, masks, and manual keyframes; use After Effects tracking when the text must attach to a moving plane or camera.

common_mistakes: Putting text over the exact subject detail the shot is built around.
Using a cute or meme font on a serious cinematic scene.
Blending text into the background so far that it becomes unreadable.
Tracking text into the scene when a simple static placement would preserve emotion.
Letting captions collide with scene-attached labels.
qc: Is the text placed in real negative space?
Does the type style match the scene's theme and emotion?
Does color temperature feel integrated while staying readable?
Does tracked text stay stable without jitter?
Do captions and scene text avoid collisions?
